Note: `toJson(Double.MAX_VALUE, float.class)` now correctly throws `IllegalArgumentException` since `Float.toString` of the narrowed value is `Infinity` (this matches the repo's tests, which only expect `Infinity` output with `serializeSpecialFloatingPointValues()`).

Summary of changes:

**`gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/internal/bind/TypeAdapters.java`** — the `write` methods of the `BYTE`, `SHORT`, `INTEGER`, `LONG`, `FLOAT`, and `DOUBLE` adapters now perform the numeric conversion (`value.byteValue()`, `shortValue()`, `intValue()`, `longValue()`, `floatValue()`, `doubleValue()`) instead of delegating to `JsonWriter.value(Number)` which just wrote `Number.toString()`, while preserving null handling (`out.value(value == null ? null : ...)`).

**`gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/Gson.java`** — the default (non-special) `doubleAdapter` and `floatAdapter` writes now write the converted primitive (`out.value(doubleValue)` / `out.value(floatValue)`) instead of the original `Number`, so narrowing conversions (e.g. a `Long` serialized as `Float`) are actually applied and validated.

The `longAdapter` in Gson.java was intentionally left unchanged since its `out.value(value.toString())` is what implements the `LongSerializationPolicy.STRING` behavior (writing longs as JSON strings).
